classification: TREATMENT-INTEGRITY finding. Does NOT invalidate any frozen evaluation.
DOES_NOT_TOUCH: their evaluation numbers -- still valid records of what those checkpoints did
how_it_was_found: SPPPO's RankingRunner cross-checks the latent label against the LIVE opponent_id every minibatch and aborts on disagreement. On its first contact with a real 32-env rollout it aborted: 'z/pole consistency violated on 40/512 rows'. This appears to be the first check in the project that ever verified z against the live opponent DURING training rather than only at construction.

mechanism.what_set_next_opponent_does: pins each env to its cell key for the FIRST episode only
mechanism.what_happens_next: when that episode ends the env RESAMPLES from the pool 50/50
mechanism.why_it_went_unseen: configure_exp2b_live_environment validates per-env z/pole exactly once, at reset. Nothing re-checked it afterwards, and neither run_exp2b_* nor run_exp2c_* sets opponent_randomize.

EXP2B.intended_cells: (16,0,0,16) ASSIGNED -- z0 should see only OP6, z1 only OP7

EXP2C.intended_cells: (16,0,0,16) ASSIGNED -- z0 should see only OP6, z1 only OP7

interpretation.EXP2: UNAFFECTED. EXP2 intended balanced (8,8,8,8) cells, so ~50/50 occupancy is its design. EXP2 remains a valid shared-latent compression failure.
interpretation.EXP2B: The defining treatment did NOT instantiate. Observed occupancy is ~50/50, statistically indistinguishable from EXP2's intended-balanced condition. EXP2B can no longer be used as strong evidence that ASSIGNED-POLE optimisation was insufficient -- assigned-pole optimisation was not what ran.
interpretation.EXP2C: Same defect. EXP2C still shows that private mode-specific heads increased behavioural separation, but it was not trained under persistent assigned-pole conditions either.
interpretation.net_effect_on_EXP2B_and_EXP2C: in pole assignment they did not differ from EXP2 at all. Their real differences were architectural/loss-side only.

historical_claim_revised.previous_story: assigned-pole training failed, then private heads also failed
historical_claim_revised.corrected_story: the intended assigned-pole treatment was never maintained past episode 1, and the first strict live z/pole check exposed it. The negative verdicts stand; the causal attribution to assigned-pole optimisation does not.

consequence_for_SPPPO: SPPPO_V1_PROTOCOL amended BEFORE any valid sweep: opponent_randomize = False for all five candidates and the 1M production run, so the frozen 16/0/0/16 treatment is actually instantiated. See SPPPO_V1_PROTOCOL.json :: AMENDMENT_ASSIGNED_POLE_PERSISTENCE.
